Maladaptive Strategies.value: Being reminded of the event by others
Being around people in authority or uniform

Threat.value: I wake during the night to check whether I am safe
I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations

vignette: Alejandro's eyes scan the street as he walks to work, his mind on high alert for any sign of danger. It's a habit that formed long ago, after the night he was taken by men in uniforms and subjected to unimaginable pain. He remembers the sound of their laughter, the feel of the cold concrete beneath him, and the smell of sweat and fear. The memories are etched into his mind like scars on his skin. Alejandro's job as a maid takes him into the homes of strangers, where he must navigate unfamiliar spaces and avoid triggering reminders of that terrible night. He steers clear of any conversation that might lead to questions about his past, fearing that someone will accidentally uncover the truth. His coworkers have grown accustomed to his quiet nature, but they can't help noticing the way he flinches when a police car drives by or a loud noise startles him. The triggers are everywhere, it seems. Similar cars drive down the street, their sleek designs and shiny exteriors transporting Alejandro back to that night. He tries to avoid watching TV or scrolling through social media, where images of torture and violence can send his mind reeling. But sometimes he catches a glimpse of something – a news report, a movie scene, a meme – and it's like being punched in the gut all over again. Alejandro has developed strategies to cope with these reminders, but they're not always effective. He smokes constantly, using the nicotine to calm his racing heart and foggy mind. He avoids talking about the event or even thinking about it too much, hoping that if he ignores the memories, they'll eventually fade away. But at night, when the darkness closes in around him, Alejandro's fears resurface. He wakes up multiple times, checking the locks on his door and scanning the shadows for potential threats. The world feels like a perilous place, full of strangers who might be lurking in wait. Alejandro is constantly on edge, bracing himself for an attack that never comes. Even when someone touches him unexpectedly – a gentle tap on the shoulder or a friendly clap on the back – he reacts with alarm, his heart racing and his senses on high alert. It's been years since the torture, but Alejandro still feels like he's living in its shadow. He's tried to move on, to build a new life for himself after the divorce, but the memories linger. His ex-wife couldn't understand why he was so distant, so guarded all the time. She thought he was just being paranoid or withdrawn, but Alejandro knew the truth – that he was fighting a war inside his own mind. The final straw came when Alejandro's boss asked him to clean a client's house on the outskirts of town. The address sounded familiar, and as he pulled up to the curb, Alejandro realized why – it was just a few blocks away from where he'd been held captive all those years ago. Something inside him snapped, and for the first time in months, he felt like he couldn't keep going. Alejandro knows that seeking help is a risk, but he can't shake the feeling that he's running out of options. He's tired of living in fear, tired of being controlled by his memories. As he sits in the therapist's office, fidgeting with his hands and avoiding eye contact, Alejandro whispers the words he's been too afraid to say aloud – "I need help. I don't want to be like this anymore."
